title: How the words show: a line, a few words, or one, with the current word popping
goal: User 2026-09-25: 'I should be able to change... even the highlight behavior (for example, maybe I want to have a sentence at a time, or 3 words at a time, or 1... maybe the current word should have a soft grow animation with a bounce to make it more obvious. There could be styles to the caption. Maybe glow on the overall text vs the active word. I want it to be easy to tweak.' Builds on the Captions layer. Compare with CapCut, Descript, Premiere's captions and Submagic styles: is it as quick to get a good look here?
acceptance: A Captions section on the Captions layer: Show (a dropdown: Sentence, Line, 3 words, 2 words, 1 word) regrouping the words live, and Lines (1 or 2)

Current word: its own row of styling separate from the rest of the text: colour, background pill, glow, scale; and an animation dropdown: None, Grow, Grow with bounce (a soft spring), Pop, Underline sweep; with the timing of the pop in a single Speed slider
Glow, shadow and stroke can be set on the whole text and separately on the current word
Words already said, the current word, and words to come can each dim or keep full colour (karaoke vs one-at-a-time)

Styles: a row of visual preset tiles (live previews of the real caption, like the transition tiles) that set all of the above in one click: e.g. Clean, Bold pop, Karaoke, Lower third, Neon; the user's own tweak can be saved as a style
Every control is a label with a control, no explanations; long option lists are dropdowns; side by side with docs/design/mocks/pages/video-captions.html
The animation renders identically in the canvas during playback and in the exported video, at 60fps without dropped frames on a 1080p recording
A walk at Next defaults switches Show to 1 word, picks Grow with bounce, adds a glow to the current word only, and photographs three moments mid-word
